As part of this task, HPE will focus on implementing an evolving anomaly detection pipeline that requires automation of the following items: • Metric identification/classification • Metric transformation • Selection of anomaly detection algorithms • Data analytics The anomaly detection pipeline will be updated as results are obtained during testing at NREL. NREL deliverables: • Use platform provided in Task 1 to host KM components. • NREL to identify key metrics to test the automated anomaly detection pipeline on. • If not otherwise available, NREL will create some manufactured events or data streams that HPE can run the real-time automated anomaly detection algorithms against. Suggestions include unplugging one or more sensors (e.g., flow meters, temperature sensors, pressure sensors), changing a set-point on a CDU, or changing a set-point on a Cooling Rack. • NREL to provide data science feedback on the algorithms, as well as feedback on operational effectiveness of the associated results of the real-time automated anomaly detection. • HPE deliverables: • HPE to create a test protocol to validate the automatic anomaly detection system. • HPE to create a python package that automatically identifies and ranks one or multiple anomaly detection pipelines for any input metric. Task 3.2.7: Facility Optimization - Power Usage Effectiveness In Year 1, NREL identified and documented all of the metrics needed to calculate the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). The next step is for NREL to ensure that all of these metrics are streamed to Kafka and stored in the ElasticSearch database. Under this task, HPE will work with NREL to first calculate the PUE in real-time, then to optimize the PUE based upon several key metrics. NREL will identify several key metrics that can be focused on for preliminary optimization of the PUE. 8 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. NREL deliverables: • NREL to ensure that all metrics needed to optimize the PUE are streamed to Kafka and stored in the ElasticSearch database. • Investigate the development of a PUE prediction model from historical data. • Advance research into the energy balance obtained from all the metrics, including IT equipment for optimizing setpoints. • Conduct initial investigation into other potential data center optimizations, such as waste heat recapture and reuse via ERE (Energy Reuse Effectiveness). HPE deliverables: HPE will create and deploy a model that predicts the PUE based on input metrics. Task 3.2.8: Predictive Scheduling of Cooling Current data center cooling management systems do not take future IT load and behavior into account. Since there is a large amount of thermal inertia built into a large data center such as NREL’s, the system can take a long time to cool down or warm up when running various applications, e.g., jobs or workloads such as WRF (Weather Research Forecasting), OpenFoam, etc. For this task, NREL will collect power footprints from all the applications that run on Eagle.
